excessive supplementation. Hyperkalemia can be seen in trauma or severe burns that lead to sig­
nificant tissue damage resulting in release of potassium into the blood. Symptoms of hyperkalemia 
include tingling in the hands and feet, muscle weakness, and temporary paralysis. Hyperkalemia 
causes characteristic EKG changes and when severe, can lead to ventricular asystole or fibrillation. 
Left untreated, hyperkalemia can result in cardiac arrest. Near fatal hyperkalemia has been seen in 
people using a nutritional supplement or a salt substitute in combination with certain medications 
such as potassium-sparing diuretics.
Supplementation Issues Potassium helps to maintain proper function of both the heart and 
nervous system. Regular consumption of high-potassium foods or potassium supplements may 
help to lower and control blood pressure in people with a high salt intake. People with heart failure 
or high blood pressure benefit from adequate amounts of this mineral. An elevated potassium 
intake has also been linked to decreasing the risk of stroke, osteoporosis, and calcium-containing 
kidney stones.

Selenium
Selenium is an essential trace mineral in the body that contributes to antioxidant defense 
mechanisms.
Form and Absorption Selenium absorption is efficient and is not regulated. Selenium in the form 
of selenocysteine and selenomethionine in the diet is absorbed in the gastrointestinal tract in the

Functions
•	 Selenium is an essential component of the enzyme glutathione peroxidase, which protects cells
